title: Starting System Specifications — 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
I use the row labels as carefully as the figures: cranking speed describes engine rotation, while current draw describes the starter’s electrical demand. Read each value with its printed unit and load condition. No-load, normal-load and maximum-load current are different comparisons; the maximum is a ceiling in the table, not a performance goal.

The cranking-speed, no-load-current and normal-load-current entries are marked as averages. The starting-circuit voltage-drop entry is also marked as an average and specifies an engine at normal operating temperature. Voltage drop is voltage used across part of a circuit while current flows. Excessive drop can reveal resistance that a no-load check misses—rather like a restriction that only becomes obvious when something has to get through.

This page provides specifications, not a complete test. Obtain equipment connections, measurement timing and the next diagnostic branch from the matching engine instructions. These figures alone cannot justify replacing the starter.

edits.why: A useful comparison matches the measurement to its load condition and preserves the average and temperature qualifiers. The maximum-load current specification must remain distinct from normal-load demand.
